title: Subject–Verb Agreement — Mastery
description: Master every subject-verb agreement rule for Grade 9: or/nor subjects, indefinite pronouns, plural-form singular nouns, 'a number of' vs 'the number of', fractions and gerunds — practice and tests.

topics.title: Or/Nor Subjects, Indefinite Pronouns & Plural-Form Singular Nouns
topics.concept:
Subjects joined by or, nor, either…or, neither…nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject.

  • Neither the players nor the coach was happy. (nearer = coach)
  • Either the coach or the players were wrong. (nearer = players)

Indefinite pronouns — everyone, someone, anyone, nobody, each, either, neither, one — take a singular verb.

  • Everyone has a role. Each of the girls is ready.
  • 'None' can be singular (formal) or plural (informal).

Nouns plural in form but singular in meaning take a singular verb: physics, mathematics, economics, news, measles. The news is good. But tools/garments in pairs are plural: scissors, trousers, glasses → The scissors are sharp.

examples.problem: Choose: Neither the boys nor the girl ___ (was/were) late.

examples.solution: are — 'scissors' is plural in form and meaning.

recap: or/nor → verb agrees with the nearer subject
Indefinite pronouns (everyone, each, neither) → singular verb

topics.title: A Number Of, Fractions, Gerunds & More
topics.concept:
A number of vs The number of:

  • A number of (= many) → plural verb: A number of students are absent.
  • The number of → singular verb: The number of students is falling.

Fractions / percentages agree with the noun after 'of':

  • Half of the cake is gone. (cake = singular)
  • Half of the apples are rotten. (apples = plural)

Gerund subjects are singular: Reading books is my hobby.

Other rules:

  • 'More than one' + singular: More than one student was absent.
  • Distances, amounts, time as a unit → singular: Ten kilometres is a long walk.
  • Titles/names as one unit → singular: 'Great Expectations' is a novel.
recap: A number of → plural; The number of → singular
Fractions/percentages agree with the noun after 'of'
Gerund subjects, units of distance/time, and titles → singular

questions.q: Spot the error: 'Neither of the two proposals are acceptable.'

questions.explanation: When members act individually, the collective noun takes a plural verb and pronoun.

options: A number of question was difficult.
A number of questions were difficult.
The number of questions were difficult.
A number of questions was difficult.

questions.q: Fill in: 'Either you or I ___ mistaken.'
Choose: '___ the captain or the players to blame?'
options: Both A and B depending on order
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer subject; here 'players' is nearer → 'Are'. (If reordered, 'Is'.)

questions.q: Identify the correct verb: 'Bread and butter ___ what I eat for breakfast.'
questions.explanation: 'Bread and butter' is one dish → singular 'is'.

questions.q: Rearrange: 'is / of / number / falling / the / births'
options: The number of births is falling.
A number of births is falling.
The number of births are falling.
Of births the number is falling.
questions.explanation: 'The number of births is falling.' is correct.

questions.q: Choose: 'Many a student ___ failed because of carelessness.'
questions.explanation: 'Many a + singular noun' takes a singular verb 'has'.

outcomes: Apply agreement with or/nor and either…or/neither…nor
Use the correct verb with indefinite pronouns
Handle nouns that are plural in form but singular in meaning
Distinguish 'a number of' and 'the number of'
Agree verbs with fractions, percentages and gerunds

intro.en: You know the basic rule: a singular subject takes a singular verb. Grade 9 is about the tricky cases that trap even good writers — subjects joined by 'nor', words like 'physics' and 'scissors', and quantities like 'a number of'. Get these right and your sentences will be flawless under exam pressure.
intro.hi: मूल नियम आप जानते हैं: एकवचन कर्ता एकवचन क्रिया लेता है। कक्षा 9 उन कठिन स्थितियों के बारे में है जो अच्छे लेखकों को भी फँसा देती हैं — 'nor' से जुड़े कर्ता, 'physics' और 'scissors' जैसे शब्द, और 'a number of' जैसी मात्राएँ। इन्हें सही कर लें तो परीक्षा-दबाव में भी आपके वाक्य निर्दोष रहेंगे।

real_life.situation:
You edit a school report:

Draft: The number of absentees are rising, and neither the teachers nor the principal were informed.

Fixed: The number of absentees is rising, and neither the teachers nor the principal was informed.
real_life.why: 'The number of' is singular → 'is'; with 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'principal' → 'was'. These are exactly the agreement traps tested at this level.

rule_box.formula: Find the real subject → then apply the special rule
rule_box.example: Mathematics is easy; the scissors are sharp; each of them is ready.

quick_test.q: 'The number of cars ___ increasing.' Which verb?
quick_test.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb ('is').

common_mistakes.note: 'A number of' takes a plural verb.

reading.passage: The number of applicants this year is record-breaking. Neither the principal nor the teachers were prepared for the rush. "Statistics is not my strong point," the clerk admitted, "but a number of forms are still unprocessed." Half of the staff was on leave, and reading through every file was exhausting. Three weeks is simply not enough time.

questions.q: Why is 'is' used in 'The number of applicants … is record-breaking'?
questions.answer: 'The number of' always takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Explain the verb in 'a number of forms are still unprocessed'.
questions.answer: 'A number of' means many, so it takes a plural verb 'are'.

questions.q: Why is 'Three weeks is … not enough' singular?
questions.answer: A period of time treated as a single unit takes a singular verb.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences using these tricky subjects with correct agreement: the news, a number of, neither…nor, a gerund subject, and a period of time.
writing.example: The news is good. A number of fans are cheering. Neither the bat nor the balls were new. Reading is my passion. Two hours is enough.
